record_notes.DCP-LETT-1648: March 17, supplied 1855 ALS. Two blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Braun translation consulted at specific pages, Godron work still unlocated despite booksellers and others; separate versus periodical publication unknown. Hornschuch extract/reference likewise sought, not actual work read. Later Natural selection citations and full modern bibliography do not supply current access. Summary 1847 versus bibliography 1848–49 remains a source-level dating discrepancy.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1658: March 31, supplied 1855 ALS. Four blocks, five footnotes and bibliography. Missing Henfrey note shows extensive search, Godron still unavailable from Paris, London or Kew; Darwin gives up for now. Hornschuch location supplied but discouraging remarks reduce desire to read, not proof of reading. Later checklist mark and acquired expanded 1859 book are distinct; apparatus inference of post-Origin access is not an exact known-by date. Possible assistance future, not invoked now.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1649: 18, supplied March 1855 ALS. Seven blocks, eleven footnotes and bibliography. Privately comments on Horner manuscript already read for referee duty. Strong doubt about Russegger baked sandstone conditional on missing mineralogical tests; will withdraw if those tests exist, not unconditional proof of error. Own superficially vitrified iron beds and officer lava misidentification compared; origin unexplained. Suggestion to shorten only geological introduction tentatively retracted/regretted, not whole-paper length condemnation. Says these criticisms excluded from report;1650 independently confirms favorable report. P7 manuscript page25 evaporation wording clarification distinct from p58 non-lamination. Later published deletion is editorial comparison, not current revision completed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1676: April 27, supplied 1855 ALS. Three blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Recalls manuscript material shortened into Volcanic islands p143; vitrified term absent from printed page though used orally. Two officers lava/lightning similes illustrate appearance, not heat mechanism accepted. Granite contact observed and heat rejected; apparatus explains mechanical interpretation separately. This is own follow-up to missing Horner exchange, not new incoming document or new examination of Egyptian rock.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1491: November 23, 1852 copy testimonial. Two blocks, two footnotes and bibliography. Commends Johnston scientific work and urges government recompense. Missing solicitation not preserved; later unsuccessful pension application and special Mantell basis remain outcomes, not knowledge at writing. Formal testimonial register is Darwin prose with inferred routing, not ordinary back-and-forth or actual award.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1531: September 6, 1853 copy. Three blocks, five footnotes and bibliography. Rare Balani received, three non-American kinds represented. Common near-Madras habitat for two loose larger specimens presumed and queried; silence would be interpreted as agreement, not independent locality proof. Flora received lately, only parts and preface read, zoological sequel hoped for. Johnston 1855 death and unfinished sequel later, not current awareness.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1429: May 26, supplied 1851 from mourning stationery. Six blocks, eight footnotes and bibliography. Missing Ball observations received, Chelonobia identification confident but mechanism and sideways movement uncertain; has not yet closely studied genus. Cast judged not worth sending while real specimens desired;1434 later cast receipt does not rewrite this preference. Requests rapid-growth South American Balanus, not received yet. Prior Thompson collections inform five British Anatifa claim. Modern taxonomy and later1852 work separate. Summary categorical nonpenetration erases expressed doubt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1434: June 8, supplied 1851 ALS. Four blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Cast and account actually received despite earlier dismissal; physical originals not thereby received. Chamber reportedly isolated from seawater deepens confusion. Adds cement injury and pressure-induced absorption hypothesis, not proven mechanism; rejects mechanical burrowing with stronger confidence. Summary says base absorbed by bone but body suggests living tissue absorption under pressure. Future study of main genera, not completed1852 dissection yet.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1445: July 24, supplied 1851 ALS. Seven blocks, six footnotes and bibliography. Requests old Newport scissors as model for Weiss after two poor pairs, recounts prior demonstration roughly two/three years earlier, exact1848 date only likely in apparatus. Last pedunculate manuscript page finished, publication and gift copy future, Ray membership unknown. Asks partly for young John Lubbock; skill versus tool quality explicitly qualified. Historical instrument-loan request does not establish loan before1450.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1450: August 12, supplied 1851 ALS. Five blocks, two footnotes and bibliography. Missing Newport note dated28th, inferred July, known by writing; exact arrival unspecified. Exhibition visited, proposed Newport visit failed. Scissors loan received and now returned; Weiss polished them, attempted sharpening only conjecture, damage feared not proved. Darwin existing pair reground appears sharper but explicitly not tested; no new pair bought. Linnean gift and Lubbock message promised, later presentation-list outcome distinct. No full incoming instructions.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1439: Missing Darwin letter before January31,1851 represented by one Palaeontographical Society council-minute block. Institutional resolution for labels, not Darwin verbatim prose. Artificial1809 lower bound not composition. Minute event and missing outgoing letter dates distinct, no evidence Darwin already knew resolution. Full available source and footnote read; authorial body unavailable.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1555: Missing Darwin letter before February24,1854 represented by two council-minute blocks and two footnotes/bibliography. Council asks completion of fossil Balanidae monograph; underlying proposal text unavailable. February24 meeting date not letter composition or receipt of council answer by Darwin. Artificial1809 lower bound not historical possibility; formal resolution not Darwin voice or preserved incoming official reply.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1565: April 6, supplied 1854 in Praeger transcription. Two blocks, five footnotes and bibliography. Answers missing March28 note after illness, remembers Thompson manuscripts returned and almost sure specimens packed; search unsuccessful but possible overlooked items admitted. Sudden memory of one returned-for-reexamination specimen strengthens belief main collection had gone back, not exact custody proof. Plans complete inventory later;1579 finds residual specimens and notes. Later September9 packing and May2 conversation are separate events, not already accomplished.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1579: August 21, supplied 1854 in Praeger transcription. Three blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Inventory now finds about half dozen Thompson specimens including bottles plus manuscript notes, contradicting any blanket inference all returned in1565. Asks shipping/accumulation instructions because glass and cost problematic. Liverpool attendance uncertain, later actual absence not current decision. No proof of dispatch or estate receipt yet.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1786: November29 in one of fourteen mutually exclusive1842–1855 dates. Three blocks, three footnotes. Missing Price letter of12th received, exact month presumed November but year unresolved. No known local schoolmaster; editorial pre1850 suggestion not hard cutoff. Serpula distinction only supposition while shell forms may conceal unrelated animals. Address use periods and encoded annual alternatives differ in precision; retain raw alternatives, no earliest-day selection. Source-wide date and period hold.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1582: 26, supplied August1854 copy. Six blocks, eight footnotes and bibliography. Price note and oilcloth specimen received; acid dissolution now shows retained color and leads Darwin to abandon extra belief that pressure checks epidermis formation. Six-week-earlier final printing means correction comes after book, not backdated into earlier beliefs. Museum deposit future, Liverpool trip conditional, help with great Balani requested for five/six months later. Possible Latin-description purpose and species identification in apparatus not explicit body request. Family illness, MissMeek kindness and house enquiry separate reported matters.

Formal favorable referee recommendation for Horner valuable observations with future value forecast. P3 explicitly Figure3 not sent, so report does not prove receipt/examination of entire visual apparatus. Contrasts private criticisms in1649 without fabricating a preserved incoming manuscript conversation. Metadata routes to Sharpey/RoyalSociety; body authorship Darwin.

visual_readings.visual_observation: B at high left and A at lower right joined by sloping upper line. A horizontal line back to left with90degree mark creates a right triangle; a curved pointer labels angle to be ascertained. Lower uneven line labelled slope of river, bottom bracket sea-level. Schematic supports indirect height/distance trigonometry, not direct clinometer observation; no numeric distances on figure.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
